definition: Prior x y is interpreted as x being required for y to exist, while y is not required for x to exist. Separate typed policies assert cause-priority to each effect-part, proper-part priority, and transitivity.
note: Rutten fn174 defines the interpretation and asserts strict partial order; p135 asserts cause-priority to EVERY effect-part. This is distinct from act/potency priority, temporal precedence and complete-cause edges. Ordinary component dependence can illustrate proper-part priority, but no independent example establishes the entire universal complete-cause-to-each-part policy. A component can overlap its whole, so Prior is not the nonoverlapping production edge. The formal primitive relation has only the explicit policies; no reality, modal, empirical or PSR bridge is certified. Humean and reciprocal-dependence readings can reject these policies; their explanatory adequacy is not settled by this theorem.
